title: Probe Budget & Tenant Cost SLA Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for tying synthetic probe budgets and live telemetry to per-tenant cost SLAs. Goal is to: (1) limit observability query/trace cost by tenant, (2) surface high-signal, low-cost metrics for operators, and (3) provide a structured runbook for diagnosing tenant cost anomalies without exploding tracing/query budget.

Context / motivation:
- Observability cost (traces, probe traffic, dashboards) has grown with more tenants and finer-grained probes. We need rules so Dev/Product teams can request higher fidelity without surprising infra/finance.
- Separate concerns: operational signal (for oncall), billing signal (for finance/CS), and investigation instrumentation (for engineers).

High-level approach:
- Define a per-tenant probe credit (monthly) derived from commit tier + recent usage. Credits purchased or auto-scaled; low credits => reduced sampling/less frequent probes.
- Classify signals into three tiers:
  * Tier A (operational): must-have, low-cardinality, high-actionability (alerts allowed).
  * Tier B (diagnostic): conditional, moderate-cardinality, buffered for investigation windows.
  * Tier C (deep-dive): high-cardinality traces, stored short-term, gated by credits.
- Default dashboard mode shows Tier A+B; Tier C only unlocked by operator flip or tenant credits.

Metric definitions (short canonical list — owners should register in Metric Registry):
1) inference.request.count
   - definition: number of inference requests accepted by gateway (per route, per-tenant)
   - granularity: 1m
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - tags: tenant, route, model, region

2) inference.tokens.generated
   - definition: total output tokens generated (per-tenant, per-model)
   - unit: tokens
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - alerts: tie to cost budget (see alert slabs)

3) kvcache.hit_ratio
   - definition: (# kv cache hits) / (# kv cache lookups) measured at model executor
   - aggregation: p50/p95 and heatmap by tenant
   - owner: serving-runtime
   - tags: tenant, model, device_type

4) batch.continuous.latency_ms
   - definition: end-to-end latency per request in continuous batching path (p50/p95/p99)
   - granularity: 1m, with quantiles computed at ingestion
   - tags: tenant, model_variant, batch_size_bin

5) fallback.model.swap_rate
   - definition: rate of automatic fallback events where request served by fallback model (per-tenant)
   - note: trace anchors must include reason code (capacity|latency|error)

6) probe.credit.balance
   - definition: remaining observability credit units for tenant (derived metric)
   - owner: observability-finance
   - tags: tenant, billing_tier

Sampling and tracing guidance:
- Default sampling: 1% full-traces globally. For Tier A signals set adaptive sampling: sample 100% for requests that triggered high-severity SLO breaches or user-facing errors.
- For per-tenant heavy hitters (top 5 tenants by tokens/min), enforce 0.5% baseline sampling + bounded session traces (limit 10 traces/min).
- Trace anchors to include: request_id, tenant_id, route, model_version, kv_cache_key_count, fallback_reason, batch_id. Keep these as top-level tags to allow lightweight correlations without full span replay.
- Sensitive fields: prompt text and user PII must be redacted before trace capture; only store prompt hashes for repro.

Dashboard layout proposal (compact default view):
- Row 1: Tenant health summary (tile per selected tenant): request rate, token rate, probe.credit.balance, kvcache.hit_ratio
- Row 2: Latency quantiles (small multiples by model variant) + batch_size distribution sparkline
- Row 3: Cost attribution snapshot (tokens per model * host unit cost) + 24h delta
- Row 4: Fallbacks + error rate breakdown (stacked bars by reason)
- Action pane (right): quick toggles to increase/decrease sampling, unlock Tier C traces for 1h (consumes credits), link to investigation runbook

Alerting slabs (cost-aware, severity + credit gating):
- INFO (slab-yellow): tenant tokens/min > baseline*2 for 10m AND probe.credit.balance > 0 (notify tenant owner Slack channel). No oncall page.
- WARN (slab-orange): sustained tokens/min > baseline*3 for 30m OR p95 latency increased > 2x baseline AND probe.credit.balance > threshold (page oncall if also impacting global SLO).
- SEV (slab-red): tokens/min spike causing cost projection to exceed monthly committed budget by >25% OR fallback.swap_rate > 1% AND public SLO breach -> page oncall and create incident. Tier C traces auto-unlocked for 1h (consumes credits).

Investigation playbook (step-by-step):
1) Check Tenant Health tile (Row 1): confirm whether request / token surge or latency drift.
2) If cost spike: run cost-attribution query (example SQL snippet):
   SELECT model, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(tokens)*model_cost_per_token as est_cost FROM telemetry.tokens WHERE tenant_id = :tenant and ts > now()-24h GROUP BY model ORDER BY est_cost desc LIMIT 10;
3) If latency spike: open small-multiple latency panel by batch_size_bin; inspect kv_cache.hit_ratio for correlated drop.
4) If fallbacks present: follow trace-anchor list filtered on fallback_reason != null (use sample rate or unlock Tier C traces if credits allow).
5) Take action: throttle tenant (temporary policy), request dedicated capacity, or ask CS to notify customer depending on root cause.

Sample lightweight queries (to store in query library):
- Top models by token consumption last 1h: "SELECT model, SUM(tokens) FROM tokens WHERE ts > now() - 1h GROUP BY model ORDER BY SUM(tokens) DESC LIMIT 20"
- Per-tenant probe credit projection: "SELECT tenant_id, probe.credit.balance, rate(tokens) FROM ..." (placeholder)

Operational guardrails / quotas:
- Default dashboard query retention 7d for Tier A signals, 3d for Tier B aggregated, 24h for Tier C full traces unless credit-expanded.
- Per-tenant trace storage hard limit: 10GB/month (modifiable via billing). Excess -> automatic downsampling of Tier C.

Open questions / tradeoffs (need decisions in next working session):
- How strict should automatic Tier C unlocking be? (auto on SEV may blow budget; maybe require manual approval + CS notification)
- How to price observability credits relative to token-based billing? flat vs proportional? Impacts CS conversations.
- Do we allow customers to opt-out of Tier A perf telemetry for privacy/regulatory reasons? If yes, what minimal signals remain for platform SLOs?

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Diego: wire metric registry entries for probe.credit.balance and fallback.model.swap_rate (JIRA-OBS-4821) - due 2026-03-17
- Anya: prototype tenant dashboard mock with action pane toggles (link PR in telemetry UI) - due 2026-03-24
- Priya (me): finalize alert slab thresholds with SRE and Finance and publish runbook v0.1 by 2026-03-31

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally terse — we want a small set of canonical metrics + a helper library of queries.
- Expect iteration after 1 pilot tenant. Save pilot logs for calibration.

References / links:
- Slack thread: #obs-probe-budgets (search for "probe credit")
- Confluence: /display/OBS/Probe+Budgets+Design (CONFLUENCE-OBS-PROBE-PLANS)

-- end of playbook --
